What is binary search and when can it be used?
candidate_answer: Binary search works on sorted data. Compare the target with the middle element, discard the half that cannot contain it and repeat until found or the range is empty. Each step halves the range, so time is O(log n).

question: What is binary search and when can it be used?
candidate_answer: Binary search is an elegant algorithm that works on any unsorted array. It checks the middle value and always discards the left half regardless of the target. It guarantees O(1) search time.

question: How would you find whether an integer array contains duplicates?
expected_answer: Insert each value into a hash set and check for membership.
candidate_answer: I can sort the array and compare adjacent elements. Equal neighbors mean a duplicate exists. Sorting costs O(n log n); the scan is O(n). If mutation is unacceptable I would sort a copy, using extra space.
